newsitem.title: GERMANY: Didier upbeat for 1997 despite Q1 loss.
newsitem.headline: Didier upbeat for 1997 despite Q1 loss.

text.p: Didier-Werke AG, the German engineering group, on Tuesday predicted 1997 earnings will at least match 1996 even though it posted a pre-tax loss of 8.8 million marks ($5.1 million) in the first quarter.
Didier said orders in its fire resistant materials division had improved since the beginning of the year, especially from the steel industry.

"For the full year 1997 the Didier management is confident regarding earnings at the Didier group and Didier-Werke AG," the company said in a mandatory statement. "It expects a profit that will be at least as high as 1996."

In 1996 Didier increased its group net profit by 12 percent to 18.5 million marks. The company, which manufactures blast furnace linings for steel mills, is majority-owned by Austria's Radex-Heraklith.
Didier said it swung to a loss in the first quarter from a profit of 0.6 million marks in the year-earlier period because income was hit by one-off restructuring costs at U.S. subsidiary NARCO.
Earnings were also hit because production at its German and west European plants was affected by a "difficult" development of orders up to the final quarter of 1996, Didier said.

Meanwhile Didier's plant division suffered from the weak construction sector while the energy and high temperature division traditionally sees a boost during the second half of the year when revenue from large plant products is booked, the statement said.
Planned restructuring measures in that division did not have an effect on earnings in the first quarter, it added.
